subsystems.name: Regolith mining and conditioning
subsystems.role: delivers a consistent feedstock — powder, sinter, or melt — to the printers.

subsystems.name: Print head and energy source
subsystems.role: fuses or melts soil into solid structure.

subsystems.name: Positioning system
subsystems.role: moves the head over the build volume with centimetre accuracy.
parts: gantry rails or long-reach robotic arm

subsystems.name: Materials refinery
subsystems.role: turns raw soil into the metals, glass and oxygen a settlement needs.
parts: metal casting or additive manufacturing unit

subsystems.name: Self-replication and parts workshop
subsystems.role: lets the factory make more of itself rather than shipping every spare from Earth.
parts: stock of Earth-imported chips and seals

subsystems.name: Swarm autonomy and control
subsystems.role: coordinates hundreds of machines with no hands-on human control.

subsystems.name: Habitat envelope
subsystems.role: the pressurised, radiation-shielded volumes people actually live in.
parts: pressure bladder or welded metal liner

buildSteps.title: Prospect the site
buildSteps.detail: Orbiters and rovers map soil chemistry, ice content, slope and radiation so the factory lands where feedstock and shelter are both available.

buildSteps.title: Land a seed factory
buildSteps.detail: A small payload — printers, robots, solar or nuclear power, and a stock of chips and seals that cannot yet be made locally — is delivered to the surface.

buildSteps.title: Mine and process soil
buildSteps.detail: Robots dig regolith, crush and sieve it, and dry out any ice, producing a graded powder.

buildSteps.title: Print simple structures first
buildSteps.detail: Low-risk items are built by laser sintering or solar concentration: landing pads, blast berms, roads and shielding mounds. These prove the process before anything pressurised is attempted.

buildSteps.title: Refine metals and glass
buildSteps.detail: Molten-regolith electrolysis splits soil into oxygen, iron, silicon and aluminium, feeding a foundry that prints structural metal and draws glass fibre.

buildSteps.title: Replicate the factory
buildSteps.detail: The workshop prints replacement arms, gantries and hoppers, and assembles new printer units — the printer count grows without new launches from Earth.

buildSteps.title: Build pressurised habitats
buildSteps.detail: With capacity proven, the swarm prints habitat shells, lines them, fits airlocks, and mounds regolith over them for radiation shielding.

buildSteps.title: Commission and expand
buildSteps.detail: Power, air, water and thermal loops are brought online and the settlement grows outward, module by module, into a town.

prerequisites.why: proven only in small laboratory and vacuum-chamber tests, never at building scale off Earth.
no machine has ever copied its own critical parts; even Earth's most self-copying 3D printers rely on bought electronics and motors.
mining and construction fleets must work for years with no real-time human control.
printing and smelting need hundreds of kilowatts continuously, day and night.
a city must recycle air, water and waste for years between resupply.

pathway.milestone: laboratory sintering and melting of regolith simulant, and 3D-printed habitat design studies
pathway.unlocks: confidence that soil can be turned into solid structure.

pathway.milestone: robotic construction of unpressurised structures on the Moon or Mars — landing pads, berms, shelters
pathway.unlocks: real data on dust, vacuum, thermal cycling and machine wear.

pathway.milestone: a seeded factory that demonstrably doubles its own printing capacity from local material
pathway.unlocks: construction that scales without a matching rise in launches from Earth.

pathway.milestone: printed, shielded settlements of thousands of people
pathway.unlocks: a self-sustaining off-world city — the necessary stepping stone before any interstellar version of the idea becomes meaningful.
